text:
alex: acme-prod hitting intermittent 429s on dedicated pool dpool-us-east-3 since ~2025-11-14T08:10Z. Customer says throughput dropped, app errors. sample curl & headers:

```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -d '{...}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1700000000
{ "error": "rate_limit_exceeded", "reason": "tenant_quota" }
```

maria: tenant_id: acme-42. I checked UI — quota override shows 100/min. Is that expected? :eyes:

alex: not expected, customer expected 10k/min. tagging @sam @kate

sam: pulling quota store... one sec

sam: DB row for tenant acme-42:

```sql
SELECT tenant_id, override_value, override_unit, updated_by, updated_at
---> acme-42 | 100 | minute | maria | 2025-11-14T07:59:03Z
```

sam: looks like override is 100 (not 10000). that would explain the 429s. did someone apply a quick limit change during the incident ops? :thinking_face:

maria: I applied a temporary limit change earlier when troubleshooting noisy neighbor reports — I thought I set 10k but must have typed 100. sorry, my bad. :grimacing:

kate: can we bump back to expected value and re-config refresh the runtime? autoscaler won't help while token-level limiter blocks requests.

john: I'll push update to rate-limiter config and force a sync.

ops-bot: config-sync started for tenant acme-42 (job 6789)

john: pushed override=10000 unit=minute, forcing in-memory reload

ops-bot: config-sync completed successfully

alex: customer confirmed errors stopped ~2 min after change. no more 429s in logs. :thumbsup:

sam: root cause: human typo when applying override in admin UI. follow-ups: add input validation to admin UI (min sensible threshold), show confirmation for decreases under baseline, and add audit alerting when override value changes by >10x.

maria: filing follow-up ticket RN-1234 for UI validation and RN-1235 for audit alerting. will own RN-1234.

kate: also recommend an automated canary check to compare runtime vs config-store values every 1m and alert on diffs.

alex: agreed. I'll email the customer with summary and apologize. Thanks everyone

acme-prod: thanks team — app is stable again, appreciate the quick fix.
